900.3.10(714).explanation: Exception RD 714 sets the minimum lot frontage and lot area at what existed when By-law 569-2013 was enacted, front and street-side setbacks of 6.0 m / 4.5 m on the named streets (Ellesmere Rd., Conlins Rd., Morrish Rd., Meadowvale Rd., Scarboro Ave., Zaph Ave., Euclid Ave., Willowlea Dr.) and 3.0 m elsewhere, a maximum lot coverage of 50 percent, a 6.0 m setback for a garage entrance that faces the street, and requires the required parking space to be in a building. No prevailing by-laws apply.

900.3.10(1424).explanation: Exception RD 1424 lets an existing detached house be converted to up to two dwelling units if the original building has at least 370 m2 of interior floor area, the secondary suite averages at least 110 m2, the building and any addition are old enough, and the exterior is not materially altered. A residential building that existed on November 7, 1978 may continue under former By-law 20623. A detached house erected before October 15, 1953 on a lot with a permitted floor space index of 0.6 may have a rear addition up to a floor space index of 0.69. High platforms may not encroach into the front or rear yard setback, and a lot with a frontage of 7.6 m or less may not have a vehicle entrance through the front wall. Former City of Toronto by-law 438-86 sections 12(2)66 and 12(2) 323 prevail, and former by-law 41-80 prevails on 216 Balmoral Ave.
